subject: Renewal: RetailFlux - holiday burst pool & prorated price lock
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@retailflux.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@retailflux.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning and holiday burst needs

Hi Hannah,

Hope you're well — RetailFlux's renewal is coming up in October and we want to discuss a structure that covers our anticipated holiday and Black Friday traffic. We are evaluating a committed plan for 12 months but need an explicit seasonal "burst pool" to avoid painful overage charges during Nov-Dec.

Quick context: Q3 trending shows a 3.2x spike historically for the holiday window; we expect to exceed our current committed tokens for at least 8 weeks. We're open to a committed base + a purchasable burst pool that is either prepaid or billed as a discounted overage.

Can Redwood provide a two-option proposal:
- Option A: 12-month commit with an agreed burst pool (prepaid or reserved) and a prorated price lock for the first 4 quarters.
- Option B: 6-month commit with higher burst credits and a higher base per-token rate, with quarterly true-ups.

Please include any finance or procurement constraints we should be aware of (PO timing, invoicing cadence). I'll loop in Legal if needed after we see the term economics.

Thanks — available for a call Wed or Thu this week.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Platform Operations
RetailFlux

Attachment: RetailFlux_Q3_usage_report.pdf (summary of peak windows)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@retailflux.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning and holiday burst needs

Hi Marta — thanks for the context and the Q3 report. Appreciate the clarity on the expected 3.2x spike.

We can absolutely model two paths. High-level proposal below — sending a worked term-sheet (attached) and a pricing model for you and procurement to review.

High-level options:

Option A — 12-month commitment (recommended for unit economics):
- Committed base: 45% of current annualized usage, billed monthly.
- Price lock: prorated rate lock applied over first 4 quarters (reduces price volatility for RetailFlux through busy season).
- Burst pool: prepaid token bucket sized for expected holiday delta (8 weeks). Burst tokens consumed first from pool; any excess billed at a discounted overage rate (25% off list).
- Quarterly true-ups: usage reconciled quarterly, with over/under applied to next invoice or converted to burst credits.
- Estimated baseline discount: 15% off hosted list at the committed level; incremental tiers at 18% (>=1.5x commit) and 20% (>=2x commit) based on annualized uplift.

Option B — 6-month commitment (shorter commitment, higher flexibility):
- Committed base: 30% of annualized usage, billed monthly.
- Burst pool: larger fraction of seasonal bucket included (prepaid 60% of expected holiday delta).
- Price lock: 2-quarter window only.
- Baseline discount: 10% at committed level; burst credits priced separately.

Questions for you so we can finalize sizing and PO timing:
1) Confirm whether RetailFlux prefers the burst pool to be prepaid (one invoice) or invoiced on drawdown.
2) Who in procurement will sign the PO and the expected PO lead time?
3) Legal point of contact for contract redlines.

Next step: attached is a first-draft term-sheet (proposed-term-sheet-v1.xlsx) and a very small worked example. Happy to hop on a 30-min call Wed 11–11:30 PT to walk through numbers.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124

Attachment: proposed-term-sheet-v1.xlsx (draft economics)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:50:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: RetailFlux renewal — margin check and suggested concessions

Hannah/Team — I ran the draft through finance assumptions. Key internal points:

- Baseline margin expectation: we can support 15% on committed volume for a 12-month term. Approvers have signaled we can stretch to 17% if we get a binding PO within 30 days and commit to a minimal uplift milestone (15% QoQ usage growth).
- Burst pool economics: prepaid pool gives us the best cash and predictability. If RetailFlux insists on on-drawdown invoicing, require a 15% premium to the prepaid equivalent.
- Discount tiers: finance is comfortable with the proposed 15% base. 20% max only if RetailFlux takes a 24-month commitment or agrees to a minimum annualized spend target.
- Billing cadence: monthly invoices with quarterly reconciliations preferred. PO timing: we need a PO 15 business days before the renewal effective date to ensure provisioning of reserved capacity.

Lauren — can you confirm whether we can accept partial prepaid (50% upfront, remainder quarterly) for the burst pool? That might be a good middle-ground for their procurement.

-David (SRE) — any constraints we should call out on the term sheet re: provisioning for a large burst pool?

Thanks,
Priyom
Sales Operations
priyom_das@redwood.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@retailflux.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Legal <legal@retailflux.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning and holiday burst needs

Hi Marta — following up with a consolidated proposal after internal review. I quoted the key points below for quick skimming and attached a redlined term sheet (term-sheet-v2.docx) plus the worked pricing model (calculated-pricing-model.csv).

Summary (short):
- Recommendation: Option A (12-month commit + prepaid seasonal burst pool) — best balance of predictability and unit cost for RetailFlux.
- Economics we can offer now: 15% baseline discount on committed units with a prepaid holiday burst pool priced at 25% discount to on-demand. If RetailFlux signs a PO within 30 days and commits to a target uplift cadence we can increase the baseline to 17% and provide a 10% rebate on unused burst tokens at year-end (applied as credit).
- If RetailFlux prefers not to prepay the burst pool, we can invoice on drawdown but will apply a 15% premium to the burst rate (to compensate for volatility).

What I need from you to finalize:
1) Confirmation on prepaid vs drawdown billing for the burst pool.
2) PO lead and expected sign date (we need 15 business days pre-effective).
3) Legal contact to start final redline (cc'd).

If that looks good, let's take 30 minutes Thursday at 10am PT to walk procurement/legal through the term-sheet and lock the PO timing. I included a short quote block below of your original ask for continuity.
